Temporary chemical sympathecticomy retarded SMG development, but that development returned to normal with age.

1) reserpine retarded SMGs by about two weeks, 2) the lesion was not consistently or reproducibly induced, 3) the lesion was associated with the presence of a large number of acinar cells with large, electron-dense secretory granules, 4) acinar cells with these granules were also present in the glands of animals that did not develop sialadenitis and 5) these cells were not found in the glands of untreated animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the sympathetic innervation in postnatal development of salivary glands.
the effects of chemical sympathecolysis on the postnatal maturation of the submandibular salivary gland.
the effects of reserpine on postnatal development and maturation of the rat submaxillary gland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reserpine retarded postnatal SMG development by a few weeks.
chemical sympathectomized SMGs develop normally, and that the sialadenitis is an inconsistent and nonreproducible finding.
chemical sympathectomized rats do not develop obstructive sialadentis, and that reserpine-treated rats do not develop sialadenitis at a rate greater than that of controls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sympathetic nervous system is not necessary for the development of the rat SMG, but that its absence does retard the development of this gland.
chemical sympathectomized glands are retarded in development by about two to three weeks, and that sialadenitis is not consistently induced by this treatment.
chemical sympathectomized animals had SMG which were smaller, but structurally similar to glands from control litter-mates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SMG is a relatively robust organ that can withstand the effects of chemical sympathecticomy, and that the gland is not a good model for the study of obstructive sialadinitis.
the rat submandiubular gland can develop in the absence of catecholamines, and that catecholamine depletion is not a necessary or sufficient cause of sialadenitis in the rat.
reserpine is a useful tool for the study of SMG development, and that the SMG can recover from the deleterious effects of catecholamine depletion.
